summary: An interactive 2D and 3D space mission design simulator that uses Earth (1.000 AU) as the launch origin and applies Hohmann transfer orbit mechanics to calculate interplanetary travel time, required delta-v, and launch windows—inspired by ISRO's fuel-efficient Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan).
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
Hohmann Orbit Planner is an interactive 2D and 3D interplanetary mission design simulator built for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. Using Planet Earth (1.000 AU) as the fixed launch origin, users select any major destination planet (Mercury through Neptune) and adjust the Low Earth Orbit (LEO) parking altitude. The app automatically applies Kepler's Third Law and Vis-Viva orbital mechanics to calculate Hohmann transfer travel time (in days, months, and years), transfer semi-major axis (AU), total required Delta-V (km/s), and planetary launch window cycles (synodic periods). It renders both a top-down 2D heliocentric trajectory animation and an interactive 3D Solar System view where users can drag to rotate, zoom, and simulate the spacecraft's departure burn.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
Astrodynamics equations are often locked behind complex engineering software. This tool makes real interplanetary mission planning visual, accessible, and intuitive for students, educators, and space enthusiasts—helping learners understand why fuel efficiency (Delta-V) and launch windows dictate real-world spaceflight timelines.

Tools, Languages & Data Used:
- Languages & Web Technologies: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas 2D, and custom 3D perspective projection math.
- Hosting & Version Control: GitHub and GitHub Pages (https://github.com).
- Scientific Data: NASA NSSDC Planetary Fact Sheet orbital radii (in AU) and solar gravitational parameters.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered:
- Real-World Mission Benchmark: Features a 1-click ISRO Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) preset that compares theoretical circular Hohmann transfer duration (258.9 days) against India's historic 2013-2014 Mars mission (298 days), highlighting practical engineering trade-offs like Earth-orbit raising burns and planetary eccentricity.
- Dual 2D + 3D Visualization: Combines a clear top-down orbital diagram with an interactive 3D heliocentric projection and a full 7-planet comparison reference table.
- Engineering Trade-Offs: Incorporates LEO parking orbit clearance (200 km to 1,000 km) to show how departure altitude affects total mission Delta-V.
